sections.h2: Why the county line matters in Erie
sections.html:
Two counties share this town. Erie occupies the southwest corner of Weld County and the eastern edge of Boulder County, and roughly 58 percent of residents live on the Weld side, 42 percent on the Boulder side. The county that holds your parcel sends the tax bill and files the deed.

Start with the tax statement or the county's online parcel search. Knowing Weld from Boulder tells you whom to phone for a payoff figure and where the closing paperwork will be recorded.

Erie uses the ZIP codes 80514 and 80516. Denver is about 25 minutes away and Boulder about 20. Broomfield lies to the south and Lafayette to the southwest.

Between the 2010 and 2020 censuses, Erie jumped 65.6 percent, from about 18,100 people to 30,038. The 2024 estimate is 38,594, and median household income is $99,804. Many local houses are therefore newer than the Colorado average.

New construction brings fewer deferred repairs but more identical homes competing for the same buyers. Suburbs growing this fast produce familiar situations:

  • an owner who gets a job offer elsewhere and cannot wait out a listing
  • heirs in another state holding an inherited house
  • a landlord worn down by managing tenants remotely
  • a borrower with a roof, floors or paint that need money

Selling directly to a cash buyer avoids showings, staging and financing contingencies, and that is mostly why people in those spots look into it.

Coal mining built Erie, and it left two legacies a seller should know about. One is age. Houses close to the original town center can have old additions, dated plumbing and wiring, and paperwork that takes more digging to assemble. Most mines had shut by 1960, and the Eagle Mine closed in 1978.

The other is water. Floods struck in 1890, 1921 and 1972, and a dike went up around Coal Creek after the last of those. A lot near the creek will draw questions from buyers and lenders about flood zone status, so learn your parcel's status before you list.

Erie gets 16.17 inches of precipitation in an average year, most in May (2.60 inches) and least in January (0.57 inches). Low rainfall does not protect a structure. Sun and wind work on roofs, gutters, decks and paint every month, and a tired roof is among the first things a buyer's inspector writes up. Someone paying cash simply lowers the offer to account for it and does not require a new roof beforehand.

Weld County treats taxes as due January 1 for the prior year. You can pay once or in two halves.

Payment optionDue date
First halfFebruary 28
Second halfJune 15
Full paymentApril 30

Partial payments are refused, and a postmark on or before the due date counts as on time. Interest on late amounts climbs by month. The first half carries 1 percent in March and 6 percent by August. Payment options are weldtax.com, a mailed check to PO Box 458, Greeley, or a visit to 1400 N 17th Avenue, Greeley.

sections.h2: If your parcel is on the Boulder side
sections.html: Boulder County parcels are billed by the Boulder County Treasurer, so check amounts with that office. Whichever county applies, the title company normally orders a certificate of taxes due and divides the year's tax at closing. Weld posts a request form for the certificate on its treasurer pages.

Because Colorado bills in arrears, you owe a share for the months you held the house this year, and any older balance must be cleared. With two counties in play, verify which treasurer will issue the certificate before the title company orders it. Picking the wrong one can cost a few days.

Behind on payments? Get a payoff number early. Interest builds every month, so the figure only grows.

sections.h2: Recording fee for a Colorado deed
sections.html: Colorado adds a documentary fee of one cent for every $100 of consideration when a deed is recorded, rounding any partial $100 up. The county clerk and recorder collects it, and a sale at or below $500 owes nothing. Your purchase contract normally names the payer, so find that line before you sign.

Have on hand your latest tax statement, mortgage payoff details if you still owe, and any flood zone information if the lot is close to Coal Creek. An inherited house needs the papers showing who may sign. On an older house, jot down when the roof, furnace and water heater were last replaced. A few lines on one page is plenty, and it makes offers easier to compare.

In a subdivision where a dozen houses share a floor plan, price and condition decide who gets the buyer. Buyers compare, and the house with the older roof or the tired carpet loses. That is the case for a fast, as-is sale if you cannot afford to renovate or do not want the months of waiting. It is also the case for a listing if your house is in good shape and you have no deadline.

Either way, be honest about the work the house needs, and gather the dates of past repairs. Buyers trust numbers more than adjectives.

A listing can work for a newer house in good condition when you have time: showings, staging, an inspection and a wait for the buyer's financing come with it. Cash suits someone relocating, an heir living out of state or a landlord ready to finish. The offer reflects what the house needs, so a worn roof or dated kitchen lowers the figure, and in return you avoid repairs and uncertainty. Ask for any offer in writing and compare what you would really keep.

sections.h2: How does a cash sale of an Erie house work?
sections.html:
The process is brief, and it is yours to stop at any step.

  • Give us the address, the condition and the timing you need.
  • The buyer reviews the property and may stop by.
  • An offer comes back, and you can accept it, counter it or turn it down.
  • The title company searches title, orders tax figures and drafts the deed.
  • You sign, the deed is recorded by the county clerk where the parcel sits, and you are paid.

No lender means no appraisal or loan approval to wait for, so title work and your preferred closing date set the pace. We make no promise about price or timing until we have seen the house.

faqs.q: Which county is Erie, Colorado in?
faqs.a: Both. Erie lies mostly in southwest Weld County (about 58 percent of residents) and partly in eastern Boulder County (about 42 percent). Your tax bill shows which county covers your parcel.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Erie house as is?
faqs.a: Yes. A cash buyer takes the house in its present state, so there is no need to repair, clean or stage. An old roof or dated kitchen shrinks the offer without blocking the sale.

faqs.q: Who pays property tax when an Erie house sells?
faqs.a: The title company usually splits it between seller and buyer at closing, using a certificate of taxes due. Because Colorado bills in arrears, the seller typically owes for the months owned. Ask your title officer for the exact split.

faqs.q: How much is the state deed fee in Colorado?
faqs.a: One cent per $100 of the sale price, paid to the county clerk and recorder when the deed is recorded. The contract decides which side pays.

faqs.q: Does being near Coal Creek affect my sale?
faqs.a: It can. Erie had major floods in 1890, 1921 and 1972, and a dike was built along Coal Creek afterward. Buyers and lenders may check flood zone status for homes near the creek, so learn your parcel's status before you sell.
